recipes.name: Pad Kee Mao
ingredients_raw: 3.5 ounces dried Thai-style rice noodles, wide (such as Chantaboon Rice Noodles)
1 serrano pepper, minced, or more to taste

steps.text: Place dry rice noodles in a bowl, cover with hot water, and let soak until white and softened, about 1 hour. Drain noodles and set aside.

Heat 1 1/2 teaspoons olive oil in a wok or large skillet over low heat. Cook and stir 2 minced garlic cloves until brown and beginning to crisp, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in soaked noodles, 1/2 teaspoon thick soy sauce, and 2 teaspoons sugar. Cook and stir until noodles have absorbed soy sauce and turned brown, about 3 minutes. Remove noodles from the skillet.

Heat remaining 1 1/2 teaspoons olive oil in the wok over low heat; stir in remaining 2 minced garlic cloves and cook until brown and beginning to crisp, 2 to 3 minutes. Raise the heat to medium-high and stir in pork, serrano pepper, basil, 1/2 teaspoon thick soy sauce, 1 teaspoon sugar, and salt. Cook and stir until pork is no longer pink and the edges of the meat are beginning to brown, about 5 minutes. Return noodles to the wok and stir in bean sprouts. Cook and stir until heated through, about 5 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pad Kee Mao
raw_recipe.description: This recipe for Thai drunken noodles is always a hit. Wide rice noodles are stir-fried with pork, peppers, basil, and garlic in a sweet, spicy dish.

review.reviewBody: I made this for Dinner today, I subbed the dried Thai-style rice noodles, wide (such as Chantaboon Rice Noodles) for regular rice noodles as I had no time to go to the Asian market, I also used 1/2 a serrano pepper instead of 2 cos the kids were going to eat it too. I added some red and yellow bell peppers to compensate for the serrano pepper reduction and for added colour. We all liked this recipe and I will be making it again, Thanks DeborahB for a great recipe!

GREAT recipe, however I changed it up a bunch. 

First - I couldn't find the fat noodles so used thing Rice Noodles, which worked fine. 
Second - I also could not find the thick soy sauce so made my own (cook on medium heat for about 3 minutes 1C Soy Sauce, 1C and 1 Tbls Spoon Brown Sugar. Let sit for a few minutes before using)
Third - I used shrimp and beef instead of pork and my veggies were Green and Red Peppers, half an onion
I also added some red chille paste at the end for some extra heat.

Loved this recipe. I did make a couple of changes. Used more pork and used a cup of bean sprouts since I needed to use them up. I have a lot of sweet basil, so I used that and as another reviewer suggested, added it with the bean sprouts. Another reviewer suggested using more thick soya, and since I added more meat and bean sprouts, I used more thick soya. I took the advice of other reviewers and made my own thick soya using molasses, soya, salt and sugar. I added a TBSP peanut butter to the sauce. I didn't have the pepper, so I heated some dry chili's in the oil before frying. I used a combination of sesame oil and vegetable oil for more authentic flavor. We enjoyed very much.

This recipe was delicious. I made mine with baked tofu I made with another recipe and it was so delicious. It definitely stands up to the Thai restaurants here. The one thing I would change is boil the noodles based on the bag directions rather than let them soak. My noodles soaked overnight and they still didn't have the needed texture. Boiling them for 5-6 minutes corrected that.

This was a fast and easy to put together, filling, tasty meal. I didn't use the wide noodles, because the thin was what I had. Also added a few veggies that needed to be used up such as a carrot, a couple of small red and yellow peppers and a few mushrooms. I also reversed the directions and cooked the veggies and meat prior to the noodles. The sauce was wonderful. I didn't feel the dish was hot at all and could have had more peppers added to it, but for my daughter, it was perfect so based on that, if you want more heat you can always add more to individual plates.

I'm giving this one four stars since I changed the recipe "a little" when I made it. I doubled the noodles, cuz I love rice noodles. I had some fresh ginger on hand so I minced about a tablespoon and split it between the noodles and the pork. Since others complained of dryness, I used a ridiculous amount of sauce (1:1 molasses: regular soy sauce). 2tbsp with the noodles and 7tbsp with the pork. Also added in 3/4 red pepper with the pork which is why I added SO much more sauce. In the end, this is one of my favorite recipes that I've tried from this site. Thanks Deb for the great mix of flavors and "template" recipe.

I made this using zucchini “noodles” instead of rice noodles. Instead of using pork, I added more vegetables, the mixture tasted somewhat bland so I added a little fish sauce and oyster sauce. I used Thai chili peppers instead of Serrano peppers. Thanks for the recipe:)

Good recipe, though I prefer to leave out the sugar, use fish sauce instead of salt and THAI-basil leaves instead of the common basil leaves. The serrano pepper is only there to give the dish a rich and spicy taste, but should not be eaten, unless you like a very spicy taste.

Absolutely delicious and it doesn't require any special or hard to find asian ingredients. I made a few changes. I didn't add the basil during cooking. I waited until right before serving the noodles to add fresh, chopped basil. I also added fresh,chopped cilantro and green onions. The fresh ingredients made a huge difference. Next time I am also going to serve with chopped peanuts.

This was really tasty. Will add some green onion and fresh cilantro at the end next time. My wife (who is Chinese) actually liked these more than I did since she has a love for rice noodles that borders on the absurd. She also claims that the pork and mushrooms (we added sliced mushrooms) should be fried up in the sauce with some fresh ginger and a little extra salt. Anyway, well done! Thank your husband for us.

The flavor is decent, but it is missing egg, which is in every Pad Kee Mao dish I've ever had. Our local restaurant also uses mushrooms and bamboo shoots in their dish, which might not be "authentic" but I love. Overall, this was pretty good, but I'm going to try it again with an egg for sure, mushrooms and bamboo shoots, possibly in place of the bean sprouts. I'm also going to try replacing some or all of the serrano pepper with chili paste.

Simple dishes invite personal touches and this good basic rice noodle and pork recipe allows all kinds of variations. For instance, I used oyster sauce and soy sauce, not having thick soy sauce. And since I love stir-fried veggies, I threw in a stalk of chopped celery; left over small zucchini and yellow squashes, chopped; some bok choy leaves, chopped; and two scallions added at the end with the bean sprouts. Yes, that's a lot of chopping, but that can be done ahead of time. Result? -- fresh flavors and tasty seasoning that makes the eater get up from the table feeling satisfied but not stuffed. Thanks for this "drunken" deliciousness!

i made twice as much of the sauces. Bean sprouts are not available out here in the sticks, and I used cabbage. I added chopped water chestnuts for more crunch. I added 3x the serrano peppers. When I can't find the noodles, I use rice. Overall a good dish.
I just made it, it came out good. However not authentic tasting in my opinion. Nevertheless my family liked it.
My hubby & I really enjoyed it!
Wow this was amazing! The only thing I did wrong was I thought I could handle three Serrano peppers, my mouth is still burning after half an hour.
I must have done something wrong. The only flavors I got were burnt molasses and heat.

Delicious!! Thank you for sharing. I replaced the Serrano peppers with 3 Thai chili’s. I also left the pork and bamboo sprouts out, and just added sliced red pepper and carrots. The sauce was very tasty. I will be making this again.
As good as or better than the best you can get in a great Thai restaurant! Really!

I threw carrots, a green bell pepper and tofu into mine since that's how I'm used to getting it at my favorite thai restaurant, it had a nice flavor but definitely not what I am used to and if you like even a little spice I would suggest more then one Serrano pepper.
